seo.title: IEEE EMBS at UCF
seo.description: The UCF student chapter of IEEE EMBS, the world's largest biomedical engineering society. Speakers, workshops, and student-built medical hardware in Orlando.

hero.eyebrow: IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
hero.headline: Biomedical engineering
hero.lede: We're the UCF student chapter of IEEE EMBS, the world's largest biomedical engineering society. Members come from across engineering to hear from people working in the field, pick up hands-on skills, and build medical devices of their own.

workSection.heading: What we're building
workSection.lede: Our project teams design, wire, and test real devices. They take new members throughout the semester, and you don't need experience to start.

pillarSection.heading: What you'll find here
pillarSection.lede: Three things the chapter runs, and what each one is for.

pillars.title: General body meetings
pillars.body: Our main event. Chapter updates, a guest speaker or a hands-on segment, and time afterward to talk with students a few years ahead of you.

pillars.title: Workshops and build teams
pillars.body: Skill sessions in soldering, instrumentation, and signal processing, plus project teams building real hardware. Come to what interests you.

pillars.title: IEEE EMBS membership
pillars.body: Joining the society gets you scholarships, member rates at EMBC, and the full EMBS journal catalog. That's what the chapter can't hand out on its own.

steps.title: Come to a meeting
steps.body: Find the next one on the calendar and show up. There's no form to fill in, and nobody asks you for dues at the door.

steps.title: Find what interests you
steps.body: Workshops, speakers, outreach, or a build team. Take what you want and skip the rest — most members do.

steps.title: Join IEEE EMBS
steps.body: Society membership opens up scholarships, conference rates, and the journals. Student rates are the lowest you'll ever be offered.

closing.heading: Come to the next meeting.
closing.body: Check the calendar, show up, and introduce yourself. You'll know within an hour whether it's for you.
